Recommended path: the Industrial Counselor (産業カウンセラー) training of the Japan Industrial Counselors Association (一般社団法人日本産業カウンセラー協会), a roughly six-month program covering mental-health promotion, career counseling, human-relations development, and active listening (傾聴) through exercises and role-playing.
An alternative for learning counseling-theory basics is study for the national Career Consultant (キャリアコンサルタント) qualification.

IT skills are required because labor work involves large-scale operational efficiency and the selection/maximization of in-house systems; without them it is hard to choose systems that match company requirements or to use them fully, and IT-specific terms can cause people to lose the thread of discussion.
For those uncomfortable with IT terminology, studying for the national IT Passport (ITパスポート) exam is recommended.
Data-aggregation skills are frequently demanded: labor staff must compile workers’ primary data and, in listed companies, may be entrusted with creating important materials for external disclosure.
For data aggregation (集計) skills in labor/HR work, proficiency in spreadsheet software such as Excel and Google Spreadsheets is essential and indispensable.
The private qualification MOS (Microsoft Office Specialist), operated by Odyssey Communications, is recommended as a way to demonstrate spreadsheet proficiency.
Labor affairs personnel (労務担当者) are expected to analyze both quantitative and qualitative data, identify issues, and present solutions as part of problem-solving (問題解決).
This problem-solving capability for labor personnel is cross-referenced to another section (ツボ 095).
The following section (ツボ 098) addresses the stance or mindset of labor affairs personnel.
Skill acquisition methods (スキルの習得方法) for workplace professionals include counseling skills and problem-solving skills, often supported by related national and private qualifications in Japan.
Problem-solving skills consist of analyzing quantitative and qualitative primary information/data, identifying issues, and proposing solutions.
Listening skills enable workers to consult with peace of mind (労働者が安心して相談できる聴くスキル).

Counseling-related qualifications include Industrial Counselor (産業カウンセラー), a private qualification implemented by the Japan Industrial Counselors Association (一般社団法人日本産業カウンセラー協会), and Career Consultant (キャリアコンサルタント), a national qualification.
IT and data skills include data aggregation skills using spreadsheet software such as Excel or Google Spreadsheets to compile primary information.
Additional IT skills involve systematizing and automating operations (オペレーションをシステム化・自動化) and maximizing the use of systems.
IT-related qualifications include IT Passport (ITパスポート), a national examination, and MOS (Microsoft Office Specialist), a private qualification operated by Odyssey Communications.
Labor/HR personnel (労務担当者) are required to possess skills for handling both people (emotions) and systems (logic).
The dual competency combines emotional/human-facing work with logical/systemic process work.

Labor/HR officers (労務担当者) must maintain an equality consciousness (平等意識) that treats all workers equally in order to care for them and protect their livelihoods; this is a core aspect of the labor function.

It is professionally unethical for an HR officer to treat employees unequally based on performance, rank, seniority, volume of voice in the company, or personal friendship. Example: proactively informing high-performer A about welfare benefits while only answering questions from underperforming B is not equal treatment.

HR officers handle highly sensitive personal data (address, contact details, salary, family information, illness and treatment) and receive work- and life-related consultations; confidentiality (守秘義務) is therefore essential so that workers can safely share information and seek advice.
The required stance is 'tight-lippedness to the grave' (墓場まで持っていく口の堅さ): secrets must be kept even after the officer is transferred out of the HR role.

HR work constantly confronts dichotomies such as management vs. workers, principle vs. exception, reason vs. emotion (理と情), concrete vs. abstract, order vs. freedom, and rights vs. duties; a one-sided stance cannot fulfill the role.
The needed balance sense (バランス感覚) is AND rather than OR: both poles of each dichotomy must be pursued and satisfied rather than one being chosen over the other.
When encountering a new theme, the constructive professional reaction is the spirit of 'Yes and' rather than 'No because'.
Two common reaction patterns appear when new proposals arise in labor/HR work: 'No because' versus 'Yes and'.

The 'No because' pattern negatively interprets constraints (high risk under labor law / 労働法, or conflict with internal regulations / 社内規程) and immediately replies 'Impossible! Because...' while listing reasons it cannot be done.
The 'Yes and' pattern first accepts the idea ('Let's do it!') then names likely challenges while persistently searching for feasible implementation methods.
Example of 'Yes and': if internal regulations themselves become the constraint, consider reviewing and revising those regulations rather than stopping.
In an era of change the required stance is 'Yes and' rather than defaulting to 'No because'.
The next key point (ツボ 099) examines the personality of labor-affairs personnel (労務担当者).
労務担当 (labor affairs / HR personnel) require four core stances: 平等意識 (equality consciousness), 口の堅さ (discretion / tight-lippedness), バランス感覚 (sense of balance), and Yes and の精神 (the spirit of Yes and).
平等意識: Do not 「区別」 (distinguish/discriminate among) workers; respond to them 「平等」 (equally).
バランス感覚: Do not treat conflicting matters as an easy 「OR」 choice; aim for simultaneous realization of both through 「AND」.
口の堅さ: Workers' personal information and consultation contents must be kept with the resolve to take them 「墓場まで持っていく」 (to the grave)—i.e., absolute, lifelong confidentiality.
Yes and の精神: Do not respond with 「No because」 (listing reasons something cannot be done); respond with 「Yes and」 (an affirmative, constructive stance that seeks how to proceed).
Stance (スタンス) is learned from the attitude/posture (姿勢) of superiors (上司) and seniors (先輩).
Stance is then transmitted onward through one's own attitude/posture to subordinates (部下) and juniors (後輩).
Key statement: スタンスは上司・先輩の姿勢から学び、部下・後輩へ姿勢で伝えていくものです (A stance is something you learn from the posture of bosses and seniors, and pass on through posture to subordinates and juniors).
Jung's personality type theory (タイプ論) describes two mental functions: Perceiving (P: 知覚) which captures information, and Judging (J: 判断) which organizes perceived information and draws conclusions.
Perceiving has two modes: Sensing (S: 感覚) which grasps things concretely as they are via the five senses, and Intuition (N: 直観) which links things to ideas, possibilities, and abstract concepts.
Judging has two modes: Thinking (T: 思考) which draws logical and objective conclusions, and Feeling (F: 感情) which emphasizes emotions, relationships, and consideration of others' situations.
The four functions S-N-T-F do not develop equally in a person; individual developmental biases among them constitute personality (性格).
Takeshi Osawa (developer of Recruit's SPI aptitude test) argued in his book that effective problem-solving requires using all four functions S-N-T-F.
The Operations Excellence role in labor/HR work requires strong Sensing (S) and Thinking (T) to process concrete tasks through correct processes in a logical, objective way.
The Rule Master role requires Intuition (N) to map concrete cases onto abstract concepts such as laws and work rules, plus Feeling (F) to reach conclusions that consider the other party's emotions.
The Strategist role requires Intuition (N) to grasp new societal trends and concepts, plus Thinking (T) to make theoretical judgments and design systems.
Proposing to management requires problem-solving ability that deploys all four functions S-N-T-F.
There is no single personality type uniquely suited to labor/HR work; every type (any combination of S-N-T-F development) has opportunities to contribute and succeed.
Self-awareness of which of one's S-N-T-F functions are most developed enables better contribution in labor/HR roles.

When applying personality-type frameworks (e.g., Jungian functions), first become aware of type bias; then actively use preferred/strong functions, deliberately train weaker functions, and collaborate with colleagues who are strong where one is weak, aiming for labor/HR practice that lets each person live as they are (個をあるがままに生かす労務).
Personality (パーソナリティ) theory is highly important in HR (人事). Besides Jung, study various other theories in order to deepen self-understanding.
The next section (ツボ 100) will consider the career of the labor-affairs practitioner.

The Zigzag Model of Problem Solving (問題解決のジグザグモデル) is a framework that cycles through complementary psychological functions (Sensing, Intuition, Thinking/logic, and Feeling) to reach more complete solutions.
S (感覚 / Sensing): Investigate the situation regarding the problem to be solved based on facts and data; obtain first-hand information from workers; keep antennas up for workplace conditions.

Logical/rational step (associated with Thinking): Select solutions that appear correct through rational and logical judgment; derive solutions based on objective criteria; create a rational plan from analysis results.
N (直観 / Intuition): Focus on possibilities and explore every method that might be useful in order to gain insight; read patterns behind the data; grasp relationships across the entire organization.
F (感情 / Feeling): Examine how the results will affect surroundings and stakeholders; decide while considering impact on the field/workplace; implement in a form that is easy for people to accept.
The model is adapted from Osawa Takeshi’s work on psychological management that utilizes individuals as they are (『個をあるがままに生かす心理学的経営』).
PHAO consists of four functions (PHAO 4つの機能).
Be aware of bias or imbalance (偏り) among those four functions.
Maintain overall balance as a whole team (チーム全体でバランスを保ちましょう).

労務担当者 (labor affairs / employee-relations specialists) can plan careers along several paths: specializing as a labor expert, expanding into broader HR toward 人事責任者 (HR director), moving into other staff functions, or joining BPO/HR-systems firms.
Specialization as a labor expert splits into 進化 (evolution) and 深化 (deepening).

Evolution (進化): sequentially advancing through three roles—オペレーションエクセレンス (OE / Operation Excellence), ルールマスター (RM / Rule Master), and ストラテジスト (ST / Strategist). People who can perform all three are scarce and therefore have very high market value.

Deepening (深化): thoroughly mastering one of those roles. Labor affairs is a required function in every organization, so careers can be deepened by long tenure at one company or by job changes that expose the person to different organization sizes and growth stages.

A second path is to expand beyond labor affairs into other HR domains (recruiting, organization development, talent development, systems, planning, etc.) and aim to become 人事責任者. 人事企画 (HR planning) and 労務 (labor affairs) are described as a particularly compatible pairing.
At HR-director level, issues become more abstract and strategic thinking is strongly required; training as a Strategist (ST) while in labor affairs particularly supports that move.

A third path is a shift to other administrative occupations such as 経理 (accounting), 法務 (legal), or 総務 (general affairs). Labor OE and RM skills are highly compatible with those functions and can lead toward heading an overall 管理本部 (administrative headquarters).
A fourth path is a move to BPO (outsourcer) firms or HR-systems companies, which constantly seek people proficient in labor-affairs practice—especially after the OE role has been deepened.

A career path for labor-affairs (労務) specialists is independent practice as a certified social insurance and labor consultant (社会保険労務士) or as a freelancer, applying experience and skills built as an in-house labor-affairs officer.
There is a growing trend of companies using external freelance talent for HR/personnel work; another option is side work or concurrent employment as a labor advisor without fully going independent.
Labor affairs is a professional occupation that demands advanced knowledge, skills, and an ethical stance (倫理観).
Because of those demands, roles such as OE, RM, and ST involve many difficulties.
After developing oneself through those roles, diverse opportunities open both inside and outside the company, making labor affairs a highly fortunate profession.
労務担当者のキャリアパスは、労務の専門家、人事責任者、管理本部長、BPO/人事システム会社、独立などの選択肢が広がっている。
進化のキャリア：OEからRM、RMからSTへと進化し続け、3つの役割すべてを満たした労務の専門家を目指す。
深化のキャリア：OE・RM・STのいずれか一つを徹底して磨き、深化させ続けた労務の専門家を目指す。
人事業務の幅を広げるキャリア：人事企画など他の人事業務へ幅を広げ、人事責任者を目指す。
独立のキャリア：労務の専門性を活かし、社会保険労務士やフリーランスとして独立する。
BPO/人事システム会社への転職：オペレーションエクセレンス（OE）を武器に、労務担当者のパートナー企業でのキャリアを歩む。
別職種への転身：労務との相性が良い法務・経理・総務など管理部門へ異動し、管理本部長を目指す。
Labor/HR personnel (労務担当者) who fulfill high-difficulty roles have infinite possibilities opening in their future.
Labor (労務) work has deep fulfillment (やりがい): the results of a labor specialist’s activities can extend beyond the organization and ripple through society as a whole (ツボ 091).

No company or organization exists without a labor role; therefore, thoroughly mastering 労務 as a specialist opens many opportunities both inside and outside the company (ツボ 100)—a major attraction of the job.
Executives should actively support labor specialists’ learning. The knowledge and skills a 労務担当者 must acquire are extremely broad and voluminous (ツボ 096, 097).
To build better organizations, executives should create growth opportunities for labor personnel, including participation in management meetings, training, and support for self-development.
Managers should recognize that they themselves are also labor personnel (労務担当者の一人).
Knowledge of labor and social insurance laws (労働社会保険諸法令) and counseling skills is extremely important for managers when leading a team (ツボ 096–098).
As the labor personnel closest to the front line, managers should feed back field voices and needs to executives and the HR department (ツボ 094, 095).
The chapter summary addresses four audiences separately: 労務担当者 (labor specialists), 経営者 (executives), マネージャー/管理職 (managers), and メンバー/すべての働く人 (all workers).
Labor affairs staff (労務担当者) work desperately every day to support the lives of all working people in the organization.

On-time monthly salary deposits with no delays, and the availability of systems that support balancing life events with work, exist only because someone in the organization is fulfilling the labor-affairs role.

A warm labor-management relationship (あたたかい労使関係) is one in which executives (経営者), labor-affairs staff (労務担当者), managers (マネージャー), and members (メンバー — all working people) mutually appreciate one another’s roles.
The intended outcome is that all parties jointly build this relationship of mutual gratitude rather than treating labor functions as invisible background work.
The results (成果) of a labor affairs officer (労務担当者) consist of improving employee experience (EX) in order to raise the energy of workers who generate business outcomes.
Goal setting for labor affairs officers should follow an OKR-style process: first thoroughly consider significance and decide Objectives, then place specific Key Results (指標).
Required actions of a labor affairs officer include being consulted by both management and workers and responding accordingly.
Trust with management is built by analyzing primary information from workers, then reporting and proposing the derived issues and solutions.
Necessary knowledge for a labor affairs officer includes labor and social insurance laws (労働社会保険諸法令), taxes, and life events (ライフイベント).
Skills a labor affairs officer should acquire include counseling, IT, data aggregation (データ集計), and problem solving.
Necessary stance (スタンス) includes equality consciousness (平等意識), confidentiality (口の堅さ), a sense of balance (バランス感覚), and a Yes-And spirit.
No particular personality type is required; awareness of which MBTI functions are developed—Sensing (S), Intuition (N), Thinking (T), or Feeling (F)—enables contribution and performance.
Career options for labor affairs officers have expanded to include labor specialist, HR manager (人事責任者), management division head (管理本部長), BPO/system company roles, and independent practice.
Author Tsuboya Kunio (坪谷邦生) transitioned from engineer to HR about 20 years ago at a 100-person IT company and was assigned new-graduate recruiting despite knowing nothing about the work.
He handled recruiting PR, information sessions, and interviews together with the company president and successfully hired 15 excellent new graduates, initially feeling he had done reasonably well.

He then designed and ran intern (内定者) training and new-employee training; interacting with sincere, highly motivated new graduates was enjoyable, they looked up to the similarly aged HR person, and he became strongly emotionally invested in their success.
Six months after the 15 were assigned to the workplace, one resigned; she had become unwell and lost a great deal of weight, in contrast to her energetic, sparkling-eyed self at joining.
Although she did not say it, the author felt as if she were confronting him with the question: 「結局、人事は、坪谷さんは私に何をしてくれたんですか？」 (“In the end, what did HR—what did you, Tsuboya-san—do for me?”).

This experience produced the strong self-awareness that he still understood nothing and needed to learn; from that day the question 「人事には、いったい何ができるのか」 (“What on earth can HR actually do?”) became the greatest professional question of his career.
The book 『図解労務入門』 (Illustrated Introduction to Labor Affairs) is presented as one of the author’s answers to that fundamental question about the real contribution of HR.

Japanese employer monthly compliance: when hiring (雇入れ), required procedures/reports are due by the 10th of the following month; when an employee leaves (離職), they are due within 10 days from the following day.
Payment of the previous month's withholding income tax (源泉徴収所得税) and specially collected resident tax (特別徴収住民税) is due by the 10th of every month.
Payment of the previous month's social insurance premiums (社会保険料) is due by the end of every month.
Employers must file a foreign worker employment status report (外国人雇用状況報告).
Related hiring procedures include social insurance and labor insurance (社会保険・労働保険) enrollment and a health checkup at the time of hiring (雇入れ時健康診断).
Ongoing HR operations include attendance management (勤怠管理) and payroll (給与), plus work related to joining and leaving the company (入退社に関する業務).
A hygiene committee (衛生委員会) must be held at workplaces that constantly employ 50 or more people.
A general annual business calendar can be used as a reference when creating a company's own operational calendar of recurring tasks and deadlines.
Japanese labor compliance items that must be publicly disclosed differ between companies with 101–300 employees and those with 301 or more employees; the distinction requires careful attention.
Employers with 50 or more regular (full-time) employees must submit a periodic health examination results report without delay.
Stress checks are required for workplaces with 50 or more regular employees.
A regulatory change takes effect on 1 April 2025 for companies exceeding 300 employees.

When an employee is hired in Japan, the employer must file 雇用保険被保険者資格取得届 (Employment Insurance Insured Person Qualification Acquisition Notification) to enroll them in employment insurance. Deadline: by the 10th of the following month. Submit to Hello Work (ハローワーク).

Social insurance enrollment (health insurance and employees' pension) requires filing 健康保険・厚生年金保険被保険者資格取得届 (Health Insurance and Employees' Pension Insurance Insured Person Qualification Acquisition Notification) with the Pension Office (年金事務所) or Health Insurance Association (健康保険組合).

Changes to health insurance dependents require 健康保険被扶養者(異動)届 and/or 国民年金第3号被保険者関係届 (National Pension Category 3 Insured Person related notification). Deadline: within 5 days. Submit to the Pension Office or Health Insurance Association.

Upon resignation, if the employee requests a 離職票 (separation notice / employment insurance leaving certificate), the employer must process it. For employees aged 59 or older, the 離職票 must be issued regardless of whether they request it. Deadline: within 10 days from the day after leaving. Submit to Hello Work.

Retirement or similar events that end social insurance coverage require filing 健康保険・厚生年金保険被保険者資格喪失届 (Health Insurance and Employees' Pension Insurance Insured Person Qualification Loss Notification) with the Pension Office.

When a work-related accident (労災) occurs, the employer must report it to the Labor Standards Inspection Office (労働基準監督署) using 労働者死傷病報告 (Worker Death/Injury/Illness Report), Form 23 or Form 24. Deadline: without delay (遅滞なく) if the absence is 4 days or more, or in case of death.

For medical treatment of a work-related injury at a designated workers' compensation hospital (労災指定病院), file 療養補償給付たる療養の給付請求書, Form 5 (様式第5号). For commuting accidents (通勤災害), use Form 16-3 instead. Submit at the designated hospital.

If treatment for a work-related injury is received at a non-designated hospital and the worker paid out of pocket, file 療養補償給付たる療養の費用請求書, Form 7 (様式第7号) to claim reimbursement. For commuting accidents, use Form 16-5. Submit to the Labor Standards Inspection Office.
To claim leave compensation benefits (休業補償給付) after 4 or more days of absence due to a work-related injury, file 休業補償給付支給請求書, Form 8 (様式第8号). For commuting accidents, use Form 16-6.
Some workers' compensation benefit claims (including leave compensation) have a filing deadline of the last day of the month following each half-year period (半期ごとの期間の翌月末日).
